author: kingpanther13
releaseNotes:
v4.5.7 - 2026-10-08
- fix: accept bestPracticeKey inside args on direct write tools (#519)
  - Fixed: with "Require Best-Practice Guide Acknowledgment" on, MCP clients that drop undeclared arguments (such as Claude Desktop) could not use the top-level write tools (backup, HSM, modes, Mode Manager, system settings, firmware update, virtual devices, package update). The acknowledgment key can now be passed inside the tool's `args` object.

v4.5.6 - 2026-10-07
- fix: Required Expression replace/restore, device swap verification, comparator rendering (#515)
  - Deleting a hub variable no longer leaves a pending delete behind that could remove a new variable of the same name later.
  - Replacing a rule's Required Expression no longer risks leaving the rule ungated: a replace that fails keeps the original expression in place.
  - Restoring a Rule Machine rule from a backup now brings back its triggers, actions and Required Expression.
  - Restoring a Basic Rule (or another non-Rule Machine app) no longer breaks its page, and an in-place restore clears settings added after the backup. Restores keep the rule's id by default; pass `preserveRuleId: false` to restore a Rule Machine rule as an exact copy with a new id (Hubitat's App Cloner).
  - Device swap now reports success correctly and describes what the hub actually does: the two devices exchange identities, and apps keep their existing device references. When only the MCP app itself uses the replaced device, the result says so.
  - Rule configs now show `<` and `<=` comparisons instead of dropping them.
  - Rule health now flags a rule whose Required Expression is switched on but empty, since that rule runs ungated.

v4.5.5 - 2026-10-06
- feat: guide-first on every write tool and per-section rotating acknowledgment keys (#501)
  - Every write tool now tells the AI to read `hub_get_tool_guide` before writing.
  - The best-practice acknowledgment key is now per guide section: a tool is unlocked only by the key of its own section (for example `hub_set_rule` needs the `set_rule_reference` key).
  - Acknowledgment keys rotate hourly and are published only inside the served guide section; the previous hour's key is still accepted.
    - Key format changed from `bps-ack-299` to `I-HAVE-READ-THE-GUIDE-<section>-<suffix>`. Clients that cached the old key must read the section again.

v4.5.4 - 2026-10-06
- feat: #431 read-gap tools — backup schedule, network settings, variable dependents, Z-Wave brand, app menu/mode metadata (#487)
  - `hub_list_backups` now includes the automatic-backup schedule (local/cloud frequency, daily time, enable flags) for whole-hub scopes; the cloud-backup password is never returned.
  - `hub_get_info` gains an opt-in `includeNetwork` flag that returns the hub's network config (IP mode, saved static IP/gateway/subnet, DNS, Ethernet autoneg, Wi-Fi SSID); the Wi-Fi password is never returned.
  - `hub_get_variable` gains an opt-in `includeDependents` flag listing the apps and rules that use the variable.
  - `hub_list_apps` (`scope='types'`) now reports each app type's menu tab (Apps/Automations/Integrations) and whether it is built-in vs community.
  - `hub_get_device` now resolves a Z-Wave device's numeric manufacturer id to a brand name.
  - `hub_get_app_config` now surfaces framework mode inputs and the app-type menu, with a per-built-in mode-gating reference in the tool guide.

v4.5.3 - 2026-10-05
- build(deps): bump gradle/actions from 6.3.0 to 6.4.0 in the github-actions group ([#507](https://github.com/kingpanther13/Hubitat-local-MCP-server/pull/507), @app/dependabot)
- feat: optional redaction of OAuth access tokens in MCP responses (#512)
  - New setting on the MCP Rule Server's Advanced page: **Hide access tokens in MCP responses**. When on, OAuth access tokens in endpoint URLs and app settings are hidden from what the server returns, including this server's own endpoint URLs and the URLs of apps such as Maker API. Off by default.
  - Rule backups no longer store Rule Machine's OAuth client credentials. Backups made before this update keep them until they rotate out.

v4.5.2 - 2026-10-05
- fix: native-app validation gaps and firmware 2.5.2 breaks (#509)
  - Rule and app editing: a multi-step page walk whose last step fails no longer runs the app's update, and action settings that are missing a required value (level, colour, colour temperature, ...) are refused before a rule is created or its actions are cleared.
  - Apps with driver-specific device pickers (for example Broadlink System Manager) can now have those pickers set, read back and restored from a backup.
  - Required text fields accept any non-empty text, as the Hubitat page does, and page navigation honours input defaults.
  - Firmware 2.5.2: hub health alerts are reported again, a pending platform update is no longer reported as "none" when the hub data cannot tell, local backup sizes and full-backup flags are listed, a full backup is never sent to the database restore, and the Zigbee channel and Z-Wave radio version are read from where the hub now reports them.

v4.5.1 - 2026-10-04
- chore: store .bat files as-is instead of normalizing line endings (#500)
- feat: mark disabled Rule Machine actions in hub_get_app_config reads (#492)
  - Rule Machine: `hub_get_app_config` now shows which actions are disabled — the action line is prefixed `[DISABLED]`, a `disabledActions` list is returned, and the action's row on the `selectActions` page carries `disabled: true`. Previously a disabled action read exactly like a live one.

v4.5.0 - 2026-10-04
- fix: watchdog purge confirms file deletes by re-listing File Manager (#496)
- feat: per-endpoint access toggles, Protected apps on the Advanced page, debug logging via the MCP log level (#497)
  - New **Enable local access** and **Enable cloud access** settings in the MCP Rule Server app let you switch off either endpoint on its own. Both stay on by default, so existing connections keep working.
    - A disabled endpoint rejects every request, even with a valid token; turning it back on restores access with the same token and URL.
    - The app page shows whether each endpoint is enabled.
  - The **Protected apps** picker moved to the app's **Advanced** page (the main page's Advanced link now mentions it). Changes still apply when you click **Done** on the main page.
  - **MCP Debug Log Level** now controls all of the server's debug output, which also shows up in the MCP log history. The old console-logging toggle is renamed **Log MCP request/response traffic** and now only logs each MCP request and response; your existing setting is kept.
